title: Cambridge IGCSE First Language English 0990/0500 — Paper 1 Reading

authority.sitting: 0990/11 May/June 2024 — Cambridge IGCSE (9–1) First Language English, Maximum Mark 80
authority.why_this_source: The board's own published mark scheme for a REAL series, in the code our student actually sits (0990, the 9–1 graded version). Top of the authority order (PEDAGOGY.md, Neil 2026-08-16).
authority.correction_2026_08_18: The first version of this file claimed no Cambridge P1 mark scheme existed for this syllabus era and cited the 0500 syllabus instead. That was WRONG, and the cause is worth recording: the search was `ls | grep _ms_` against the 160-file 'Past Papers (mirror 2020-2026)' folder — which really does hold only question papers and inserts — plus an `mdfind` whose output was read to 20 lines and no further. The real mark schemes sit in a SEPARATE folder under a different naming convention. Root CLAUDE.md §17c: a truncated search is not a zero.
authority.0990_vs_0500: MEASURED, not assumed (2026-08-18): the 0500 and 0990 June 2024 Paper 1 mark schemes state identical AO tariffs — R1/R2/R5 (25), R1/R2/R4 (25), R1/R2/R3 (15), W2/W3 (5). The two syllabuses differ in grading scale (A*–G vs 9–1), not in assessment. Either may be cited for tariffs; 0990 is cited because it is the code the student is entered for.
authority.secondary: research/cambridge-igcse/0500-syllabus-2024-2026.pdf splits Q1 into comprehension (15) + summary (10) and Q2 into short-answer (10) + language task (15). The mark scheme aggregates each to 25, so that finer split is syllabus-only and is not gated here.

questions.why_no_marks_quote: The mark scheme states Q1's reading and writing allocations separately and never prints 30. It is the sum of two quoted parts.
